questions.stem: Lines $y=2 \left(2 x - 3\right)$ and $y=- 2 \left(2 x - 13\right)$ meet at $P$. A line through $P$ is parallel to the segment joining $A(1, 2)$ to $B(6, -2)$. Find its $x$-intercept.
workedSolutionSteps: Solve the two given lines to get $P=(4,10)$. The gradient of $AB$ is $\dfrac{-4}{5}=- \frac{4}{5}$.
The line through $P$ has the same gradient. Put $y=0$ in $y-10=- \frac{4}{5}(x-4)$, giving $x=\frac{33}{2}$.
Set $z=y-1$, giving $z(x+6)=4x+5$.
Collect $x$: $(1z-4)x=5-6z$, then replace $z=y-1$ to obtain $x=- \frac{6 y - 11}{y - 5}$.

questions.stem: A factory makes $8\times 10^{7}$ g of material. During processing $5\times 10^{6}$ g is discarded. The remainder is divided equally into 4 containers. What mass (g) is in each container? Give your answer in standard form.
workedSolutionSteps: Subtract the waste: $(8-0.5)\times 10^{7}$ g remains.
Divide by 4 equal containers: $1.875\times 10^{7}$ g each.
Convert everything to base 2, then square: $(2^{2(2)-3(1)})^2=2^{2}$.
Dividing by $2^{-2}$ adds 2 to the exponent: $2+2=4$, giving $16$.

questions.stem: Make $x$ the subject of $\dfrac{1}{y}=\dfrac{3}{4x+3}+2$. Assume all denominators are non-zero.
workedSolutionSteps: Subtract 2: $\dfrac{1}{y}-2=\dfrac{3}{4x+3}$.
Invert and isolate $x$: $4x+3=\dfrac{3}{1/y-2}$, so $x=- \frac{3 \left(3 y - 1\right)}{4 \left(2 y - 1\right)}$ (also requiring $1/y\ne 2$).

questions.stem: A sample contains $2\times 10^{11}$ particles, each of mass $3\times 10^{-7}$ g. A filter removes $25\%$ of the total mass. The remainder occupies $1.5\times 10^{2}$ cm$^3$. Find its density in g/cm$^3$ in standard form.
workedSolutionSteps: Total mass $=(2\times 10^{11})(3\times 10^{-7})=6\times10^{4}$ g; after removing $25\%$, the mass is $4.5\times10^{4}$ g.
Density $=\dfrac{4.5\times10^{4}}{1.5\times10^{2}}=3\times 10^{2}$ g/cm$^3$.

questions.stem: Find $n$ such that $\dfrac{\sqrt{2^{2n+6}}\times16^{n-1}}{8^{n-2}}=2^{9}$, and then give $n^2-n$.
workedSolutionSteps: Express all terms as base $2$: the left-hand exponent is $(n+3)+4(n-1)-3(n-2)=2n+5$.
So $2n+5=9$ and $n=2$. Finally $n^2-n=2$.

questions.stem: For what value of $k$ do the equations $\begin{cases} 2x+3y=7\\ kx+6y=15\end{cases}$ have **no solution**?
workedSolutionSteps: To have no solution, the two lines must be parallel: the coefficient of $y$ doubles, so $k=2(2)=4$.
The constants do not double: $2(7)=14\ne 15$, so the lines are distinct and never intersect.

questions.stem: The perpendicular bisector of $A(1, 4)$ and $B(5, 6)$ meets $y=3 \left(x - 3\right)$ at $P$. Find $x_P+y_P$.
workedSolutionSteps: The midpoint is $(3,5)$, and the perpendicular-bisector gradient is $-2$. Hence its equation is $y=11 - 2 x$.
Intersect with $y=3 \left(x - 3\right)$ to obtain $P=(4,3)$. Thus $x_P+y_P=7$.
Eliminate a variable from the two equations to get $x=4$ and $y=3$.
